children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar but may be weighed by higher oil prices which typically hurt currencies of net energy-importing countries in Asia. Higher crude prices amid ongoing geopolitical risks have supported the dollar, CBA's Samara Hammoud says in a research report. "According to a U.S. official, the Pentagon may soon deploy an additional aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf," the international economist and currency strategist notes. "The move would give U.S. commanders more options should President Trump choose to escalate attacks on Iran," Hammoud adds. The dollar edges 0.1% higher to 1,360.09 won, but is 0.1% lower at 157.86 yen, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
